subject: Audit ingest format alignment & BYOK metadata questions
messages:
From: Timothy Ellison <timothy.ellison@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit ingest: SIEM schema + BYOK clarifications

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. We're working toward our SOC2 readiness window and need to validate Redwood's audit export format and BYOK metadata so our SIEM ingest can parse events correctly. Attached are two artifacts from our security team: acme-siem-schema.json (fields we expect) and acme-kms-requirements.pdf (key provenance + rotation requirements).

Top questions:
- Can you provide a sample audit export (ndjson/JSONL) with the fields in acme-siem-schema.json?
- Do exported records include KMS metadata (key_id, key_origin/arn, rotation_ts)? If not, can you provide an ingestion-friendly mapping?
- What's Redwood's retention for audit logs by default, and can that be extended to 13 months for customers in our contract?
- For SSO tracing, we need an SSO session id or method in each event (okta/google/oidc). Is that present in exported rows?

We'd like to avoid scope creep: a short sample export and quick call to align would be ideal.

Thanks,
Timothy Ellison
Head of Security, Acme Health
acme-sec@acme.com

Attachments: acme-siem-schema.json, acme-kms-requirements.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Timothy — thanks for the note and the artifacts. Looping in Jonas (security) and Marissa (compliance) to triage.

Quick plan: 
1) I'll attach a 1k-line sample export (redwood-sample-audit-v1.ndjson) showing fields we typically include.
2) Jonas + Marissa — please review acme-siem-schema.json and call out any missing fields and the minimally viable mapping for ingest.
3) If we have gaps (e.g., key_origin or rotation_ts), we can either: a) produce a schema update (2-week engineering change) or b) provide an evidence package + temporary exception while we deliver the schema.
4) Retention: default hosted export retention is 90 days; we do have contract add-ons for 12/13 months in Dedicated or via export pipeline.

Can we do a 30-min call today or tomorrow to confirm environment (hosted vs dedicated) and acceptance criteria? Proposed times: 3pm PT today or 10am PT tomorrow.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security (Redwood)

Attachment: redwood-sample-audit-v1.ndjson

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Prioym Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Mar 2028 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit ingest: SIEM schema + BYOK clarifications

Kimberly — quick technical read: I reviewed acme-siem-schema.json and compared against our audit-stream exports. High-level: we cover the majority of request/session fields (timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, user_email, sso_method), but we do NOT currently export the following fields Acme expects: key_origin (external_kms_arn), kms_key_rotation_ts, and explicit key_provisioner identity. We also don't surface a discrete field for long-lived key provenance when customers use BYOK.

Options (trade-offs):
- Option A: Export schema enhancement (recommended long-term). Add fields: external_kms_arn, kms_key_rotation_ts, key_provisioner. Implementation estimate: 2-week minor release + 1-week QA.
- Option B: Evidence/exemption path for initial SOC2: provide a signed attestation + a scheduled ndjson export containing supplemental metadata (we can inject kms metadata from our keystore audit) for up to 30 days while the schema change ships.

Retention: Acme wants 13 months. Our hosted retention is 90 days; Dedicated can be configured longer. Short-term workaround: full exports to S3 (monthly) for off-platform retention (we can securely deliver and rotate access).

Action items:
- Kimberly: confirm whether Acme is on Hosted or Dedicated (affects retention options).
- Prioym: validate whether keystore audit contains external_kms_arn to include in supplemental export.
- Marissa: flag any compliance gating items if we take the exception path (attestation language).

Related: HubSpot: HS-4821. If we pursue an exception, we should put the exception approval doc into the deal.

Attachment: sample_export_v1.ndjson

Jonas
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood

From: Prioym Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Mar 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit ingest: SIEM schema + BYOK clarifications

Adding a BYOK ops perspective. Short answers and a suggested hybrid workaround: 

- BYOK metadata: Our keystore logs include key_id and rotation history, but only show external_kms_arn for Dedicated BYOK flows where the customer-managed key was registered with an ARN. For hosted BYOK (customer uploads a wrapped key), we currently surface key_id but not the external ARN.
- Legal/provenance risk: putting an external_arn in logs for hosted customers without direct registration could create a false provenance signal; we need to be explicit in field naming (e.g., kms_external_reference vs kms_managed_by_redwood).

Suggested hybrid workaround for Acme (fast):
1) Produce an augmented export: base audit rows + supplemental metadata file (ndjson) that includes key_provenance entries tied to request_id. We can deliver this over S3 with short-term signed access.
2) Ship a schema change in the next minor (2 weeks) to add kms_external_reference and kms_key_rotation_ts to default export.
3) If Acme requires 13-month retention, route monthly exports to a secure S3 bucket that we provision and grant the Acme security team read-only access; rotate presigned URLs per month.

Risk callouts: we must ensure that supplemental metadata is marked as derived and contain clear field descriptions to avoid regulatory confusion. Also coordinate with Legal on wording if we provide attestation.

I'll validate the keystore audit output and confirm whether external ARN is present for this customer flow (estimating 24h).

—Prioym
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood

To: Timothy Ellison <timothy.ellison@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Audit ingest: SIEM schema + BYOK clarifications

Timothy — thanks for the patience. Summary and proposed mutual action plan below. Please confirm whether Acme is on Hosted or Dedicated so we can finalize the retention approach.

Summary of gaps we found:
- Missing fields in current export: external_kms_arn, kms_key_rotation_ts, key_provisioner_identity.
- Hosted retention default is 90 days; Acme needs 13 months — possible via Dedicated or monthly exports to secure S3.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
1) Today: short 30-min call to confirm environment and acceptance criteria. (Can do 4pm PT today or 10am PT tomorrow.)
2) Within 24h: Prioym will confirm whether our keystore audit contains external_arn metadata for your onboarding flow.
3) Within 3 business days: We will deliver an augmented supplemental export (ndjson) containing KMS metadata mapped to request_id for immediate ingest. Delivery: secure S3 + presigned urls.
4) Within 2–3 weeks: Engineering will ship a minor release adding external_kms_arn and kms_key_rotation_ts to the standard audit export.
5) Retention: If Acme is on Dedicated, we can set 13-month retention. If Hosted, we will deliver monthly exports to meet contract obligations while we discuss a longer-term committed retention option.

Artifacts: I attached redwood-sample-audit-v1.ndjson (example rows) and linked our working doc: https://drive.google.com/redwood/acme-audit-ingest-v1. HubSpot: HS-4821.

Please reply with environment (Hosted/Dedicated) and preferred time for a short call. If happy with the plan, we'll draft a short exception/attestation package for your compliance team.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security, Redwood
